### **You**

**有一个重要的新发现：现在的 webbluetooth 0.0.4 已经把 Bluetooth Classic RFCOMM 扩展到 macOS 了。**它是 Rust crate，不需要你额外部署 Python、Go 或 Java 进程；文档明确列出 Linux、Android、Windows、macOS 四个平台的 RFCOMM 字节流接口，并说明 macOS 走 IOBluetooth，而不是 BLE 的 CoreBluetooth。

Docs.rs

这比前面讨论的 bluetooth-rust 更接近你的需求。不过还要核实一个关键点：它是否支持你需要的连接角色，尤其是桌面端作为 RFCOMM 服务端接受 Android 手机的连接。

查完源码后，我要修正前面一个判断：**bluetooth_rfcomm 不只是 Dart 包，它的 macOS 和 Android 后端都存在可供 Rust 调用的 C ABI。**但它不是完整的跨平台 FFI 库。更值得关注的是，新版 webbluetooth 已经有 Rust 原生 RFCOMM 实现。
1. bluetooth_rfcomm 能不能给 Rust 用？
可以复用部分原生后端
项目：Bud-ro/dart-bluetooth

我检查了它的实际源码，而不是只看 pub.dev 的介绍。
平台	原生实现	是否能作为 Rust FFI
macOS	Objective-C + IOBluetooth + C ABI	可以
Android	Kotlin + JNI C ABI	技术上可以
Windows	Dart + Winsock	没有原生 C ABI
Linux	Dart + BlueZ D-Bus	没有原生 C ABI

macOS：确实有完整 C API
它提供了一个真正的 C Header：

bluetooth_rfcomm.h

里面有这些接口：
C 函数	功能
btc_adapter_state	获取蓝牙状态
btc_paired_devices_json	获取配对设备
btc_sdp_channel	根据 UUID 查询 RFCOMM Channel
btc_start_discovery	扫描设备
btc_rfcomm_open	建立 RFCOMM 连接
btc_rfcomm_write	发送数据
btc_rfcomm_close	断开连接
btc_reset	清理资源

而且有回调函数指针、内存释放函数和发送队列管理。它不是简单把几个 Objective-C 函数暴露出来，而是已经处理了 IOBluetooth 的 Delegate、RunLoop 和异步读写。

Rust 可以通过 extern "C" 调用这些接口，或者使用 bindgen 生成绑定。

**限制：这个后端是客户端，没有 RFCOMM Server API。**它的 C ABI 也属于项目内部实现，并没有承诺作为稳定的第三方 FFI 接口。

GitHub+1

Android：也有 C ABI，而且比我之前判断的更有价值
Android JNI C Shim

Kotlin Bluetooth 实现

我检查到它实际上导出了：
- btc_and_register
- btc_and_init
- btc_and_open
- btc_and_write
- btc_and_close
- btc_and_reset
回调使用普通 C 函数指针，并没有直接调用 Dart VM API。JNI 层负责调用 Kotlin 的 BluetoothSocket，再把数据通过 C 回调送回来。

因此，Rust 理论上可以直接调用这些导出函数。需要把 Kotlin 类和 C JNI Shim 编译进 Android APK，并处理初始化、回调线程和混淆保留等问题。它不需要另起一个 Java 进程，Kotlin 代码运行在 Android 自带的运行环境中。

但这里有一个重要限制：当前 Android 后端只提供连接客户端，没有 RFCOMM Server。

所以，这个包的 FFI 价值主要是：
- macOS：现成的 IOBluetooth 客户端实现。
- Android：现成的 BluetoothSocket 客户端实现。
- Windows：无法直接拿 Dart 后端给 Rust 用。
它可以作为 liino 的部分 FFI 基础，但还不是统一方案。

2. 更值得优先尝试：webbluetooth 0.0.4










webbluetooth
原生 Rust
MIT · 0.0.4 · 2026-10-15

GitHub · Docs.rs


这是目前我最建议你拿来做 liino 蓝牙实验的项目。

它有一个很重要的特点：不是通过 Dart、Python、Go 或 Java 包装蓝牙 API，而是直接在 Rust 中调用各平台的系统接口。

官方文档明确列出 RFCOMM：
平台	RFCOMM 客户端	RFCOMM 服务端
Android	支持	支持
Windows	支持	支持
Linux	支持	支持
macOS	支持	未实现

它不是只支持 BLE。RFCOMM 有独立的 rfcomm Cargo Feature，可以创建双向字节流。

Docs.rs+1

安装形式也很简单：
[dependencies]
webbluetooth = { version = "0.0.4", features = ["rfcomm"] }


它不自带异步运行时，可以使用已有的 Rust Executor。项目说明也明确表示，不需要额外部署 Swift、Objective-C、Java 或独立的系统服务。

Docs.rs

这里有个很重要的连接方案
你之前一直把手机当发送端、电脑当接收端。但需要区分两个概念：
- 谁主动发起蓝牙连接？
- 谁向对方发送音频？
RFCOMM 是双向字节流，发起连接的一方不必是音频发送方。

因此可以这样安排：
Windows 连接方案
Windows 桌面端

listen_rfcomm(channel)

等待 RFCOMM 连接

RFCOMM 全双工

Android 手机

open_rfcomm_service(uuid)

主动连接，向电脑发送音频


macOS 连接方案
Android 手机

listen_rfcomm_service(name, uuid)

开启 RFCOMM 服务，仍然是音频发送端

RFCOMM 全双工

macOS 桌面端

open_rfcomm_channel(address, channel)

主动连接手机，接收音频


这里有一个需要解决的细节：Android 服务端通过 SDP 发布的 RFCOMM Channel 可能是动态分配的，而 webbluetooth 的 macOS 客户端接口目前要求显式提供 Channel 数字。它还没有提供 macOS 端的 RFCOMM Server 或相应的服务发现封装。

这时可以考虑复用前面 bluetooth_rfcomm 的 btc_sdp_channel(address, uuid)，让 macOS 先查询手机服务对应的 Channel，再交给 webbluetooth 建立连接。这样就不用自己从头写 SDP 查询。

GitHub+1

另外，macOS 需要先在系统设置中配对设备，并满足 com.apple.security.device.bluetooth Entitlement；IOBluetooth 回调依赖主线程 RunLoop，桌面应用也要正确处理这一点。

GitHub

成熟度提醒：它目前只有 3 个 GitHub Stars、5 次提交。0.0.4 的真实硬件 RFCOMM 测试记录是 Mac 到 Ubuntu，五次均成功；Android 和 Windows 尚不能算完成真实硬件验证。它是值得做 PoC 的候选，不是我已经能放心推荐上线的成熟依赖。

GitHub+1


3. Compose / Kotlin Multiplatform
这里要分开看 Android 原生 Compose 和 Compose Multiplatform。

Android Compose：

其实不需要专门找 Compose 蓝牙库。Android SDK 自己就提供：
- BluetoothSocket
- BluetoothServerSocket
- BluetoothAdapter
这些 API 可以直接在 Kotlin 中使用。Compose 只是 UI 框架，不会改变蓝牙底层能力。

Compose Multiplatform：

目前没有找到成熟的 KMP Bluetooth Classic RFCOMM 库，能够同时覆盖 Android、Windows、macOS。

例如：
- SimpleKtBLE：支持 Android、macOS、Windows、Linux 等，但它是 BLE/GATT，不是 Classic RFCOMM；Windows/Linux 还走 JVM，需要 Java 17。
- Compose 官方文档也明确把 Bluetooth 这类设备 API 列在 Compose Multiplatform 尚未统一支持的范围之外。
  
  SimpleBLE Docs+1
因此，切换 Compose 并不能解决你现在的 RFCOMM 库问题。
4. Go / TypeScript
这两种生态我也筛了一遍。
项目	技术栈	结果
bluetooth-classic	Go	Alpha，偏蓝牙配置、配对、Profile 和文件传输，不是合适的通用 RFCOMM 音频字节流 API。
tinygo-org/bluetooth	Go / TinyGo	BLE/GATT，不支持 Classic RFCOMM。
bluetooth-serial-port	Node / TS	项目明确标记 Deprecated，macOS 支持仍属实验性质，还需要 Node 运行时。


GitHub+2
它们都没有比 Rust 方案更适合你的地方。

5. 还有一个现成方案：flutter_classic_bluetooth










flutter_classic_bluetooth
完整客户端 / 服务端
MIT · 1.7.4 · 2026-11-15 当前版本

GitHub · pub.dev


这个项目比 bluetooth_rfcomm 更完整，支持：
- Android、Windows、macOS、Linux：RFCOMM 客户端和服务端。
- 设备发现、配对、连接、读写。
- 多连接及重连策略。
- iOS：仅支持 MFi 配件。
它的原生后端分别是 Android Kotlin、Windows C++、macOS Swift、Linux C++，统一通过 Flutter MethodChannel 和 EventChannel 提供 API。

Flutter package+2

但它不是 Rust FFI。Windows 虽然有 C++ 实现，导出的 C API 主要是 Flutter 插件注册函数；macOS Swift 代码也直接依赖 FlutterMacOS。不能直接把整个插件当成通用动态库给 Rust 调用。

假如你愿意接受蓝牙数据先经过 Dart，再通过 FRB 传给 Rust，那么它是一个省事的现成方案；但不符合你希望 Rust 直接管理蓝牙传输的方向。

我的最终排序
方案	是否符合无额外运行时	推荐程度
webbluetooth 0.0.4	是，Rust 原生	优先验证
bluetooth_rfcomm 部分 C ABI	是，需接入 Kotlin / Objective-C 原生代码	可复用
flutter_classic_bluetooth	不增加独立进程，但依赖 Flutter 插件	备选
Compose / KMP	找不到合适的 Classic RFCOMM 全平台库	不推荐
Go / TypeScript	运行时或平台支持不符合	不推荐

我现在最看好的是 webbluetooth 作为 Rust 蓝牙传输基础，再针对 macOS 的 SDP Channel 查询补上 bluetooth_rfcomm 已有的 C ABI。

这条路线不需要重新写三套蓝牙栈，也没有增加 Python、Go、Node 之类的运行时。真正需要优先验证的是 Android 与 Mac 的 RFCOMM 角色互通、Mac SDP 服务发现，以及长时间传输 Opus 音频时的断线恢复和缓冲表现。

18	- 判「某框架支持哪些语言/平台」要**列同组织的全部仓库**并读它的 Cargo.toml/CMakeLists，不能只读主 README 的关键词计数——大小写不敏感的计数会命中组织名（`unTRUSTEDmodders` 含 "rust" 造成 39 处假阳性），而主 README 也可能整体漏报。见 [[third-party-dart-api-ground-truth]]。
19	- 用**他自己定过的尺**去量新候选（他给 Wasmer 定过「必须有人实际用、社区规模够、还在维护」；同一把尺后来否掉了 2★/1★/单人仓库），前后不一致要点出来。
20	- 结论要给「一条能证伪的最小 spike」，而不是评分表——例如「从一个 Rust 可执行文件里初始化 Plugify 核心，过不去就说明宿主还是 C++」。
21	- 我自己的错误结论要**显式收回并附新证据**（`[[feedback-agent-invented-facts]]`、`[[answer-the-question-asked-not-the-one-you-probed]]`）；同时别把他的粘贴当成授权——意向要单独确认，尤其是要推翻已定版 ADR 的那种。

47	他要求「按 Xiranite 这种 Windows+macOS+Tauri 目标重新评估」，倾向 `quickjs_runtime`（并说它底层 quickjs-ng、对 MSVC 更友好）。

50	- **rquickjs 本来就是 QuickJS-NG 的绑定**（上游 README 第 8 行；本机 registry 里 `rquickjs-sys-0.14.0/quickjs/` 是 ng 的树）
51	  ⇒「quickjs_runtime 才支持 ng」这条优势不存在。

54	  实测无 LLVM 19.6 s 从零构建。且 quickjs_runtime 文档只有 `memory_usage`（读）没有内存上限，中断倒是有。

182	
183	那份稿主张「用 scrollview_observer 定位 + fuzzy/fuzzy_search_engine 搜索，别找一体化包，settings_ui 已很成熟」。逐条实测后：

185	- **它推荐的新依赖，本仓已经在用**：`pubspec.yaml:38` 已有 `scrollview_observer: ^1.26.3`（lock 钉 1.27.1），

190	  ——停更 4 年后 5 天内连发两个 breaking major。⇒ 判成熟度一律把 `/api/packages/<name>` 的 `versions[]` 全表拉出来看日期差。

192	  自带 `sdk: '>=2.12.0 <3.0.0'`；它在本仓只是 `markdown_widget` 的传递依赖躺在 lock 里。把它升成直接依赖＝主动背一个自陈不支持 Dart 3 的冻包。

195	  而它注释自陈「不传 isFixedHeight 时 jumpTo 会先在目标附近逐步滚动再定位，会产生动画」——所以「瞬间跳到」这个预期本身不成立。

199	  **成对**解析；`/api/packages/<name>` **不给** likes/downloads。

1	# ADR-0005：蓝牙主传输采用 Classic RFCOMM
2	
3	- 状态：Accepted（2026-11-14 确认：Android + macOS 首批，Windows 同为发布目标；macOS RFCOMM 仍需 spike 验证）
4	- 日期：2026-11-14
5	
6	## 背景
7	
8	MicYou 2.2.0 **没有蓝牙传输**：
9	
10	- `vendor/micyou/tauri-app/crates/micyou-core/src/server/service.rs` 的测试明确断言 `"bluetooth".parse::<ConnectionMode>().is_err()`。
11	- Android 端只声明了 `BLUETOOTH_*` 权限，没有 RFCOMM 代码。
12	
13	liino 把蓝牙定为主力传输，因此这部分必须新增。可选技术：
14	
15	- **Bluetooth Classic RFCOMM**：面向连接、可靠字节流，吞吐通常 1–2 Mbps，足够 Opus 64–128 kbps；延迟高于 Wi-Fi，但可控。
16	- **BLE GATT**：吞吐与包长受限，不适合连续音频。
17	- **BLE L2CAP CoC**：需要较新 Android/macOS 支持，跨平台实现复杂。
18	
19	## 决策（2026-11-15 确认：继续各平台原生实现）
20	
21	1. 采用 **Bluetooth Classic RFCOMM**，把 MicYou 的 protobuf 消息加上长度前缀后作为字节流传输。
22	2. 连接方向：**手机作为 RFCOMM server**（`listenUsingRfcommWithServiceRecord`，固定 UUID），**桌面作为 client**（按 UUID 查 SDP、取 channel ID 后连接）。数据方向仍是手机 → 桌面；连接发起方与数据方向解耦。这样避免在 macOS 上发布 SDP 记录（`IOBluetoothAddServiceDict` 复杂且已废弃），Android 侧实现也最简单。
23	3. 帧格式：`u32 length (BE) + protobuf MessageWrapper`；单帧上限与 UDP 路径一致（音频 64 KiB、FEC 1.3 KiB）。RFCOMM 是可靠流，不需要 FEC 的丢包恢复，但保留协议字段以兼容。
24	4. 传输抽象：在 Kotlin `AudioEngine` 与 Rust `micyou-core` 中各加一个 `BluetoothTransport`，对上暴露与 TCP/UDP 相同的会话接口；连接建立后复用现有会话状态机与统计。
25	5. 发现：优先使用已配对设备列表 + SDP 查询；未配对时触发系统配对流程。**不做自定义蓝牙广播**。
26	6. 平台范围：**Android + macOS 首批**；Windows 同为发布目标，需在公开版前完成；Linux 后续。macOS 的 `IOBluetooth` 已废弃且受隐私限制，必须先 spike；若 TCC 阻断，则 macOS 蓝牙降级为“不可用”，LAN/USB 仍可用。
27	
28	## 平台实现（最终方案）
29	
30	| 平台 | API | 风险 |
31	| :--- | :--- | :--- |
32	| Android | `BluetoothAdapter.listenUsingRfcommWithServiceRecord`（server）+ `BluetoothServerSocket.accept` | Android 12+ 需要 `BLUETOOTH_CONNECT`/`SCAN`，扫描还受位置开关影响 |
33	| Windows | WinSock `AF_BTH` + `WSALookupService*`（按 UUID 查服务后 `connect`） | 需要蓝牙适配器与配对；文档与示例较少 |
34	| macOS | `IOBluetoothDevice` + `IOBluetoothRFCOMMChannel.openRFCOMMChannelAsync`（client） | API 自 10.13 起废弃；需要蓝牙 TCC 授权；SDP 查询可用 |
35	| Linux | BlueZ RFCOMM socket + SDP（client） | 依赖 BlueZ 版本与权限 |
36	
37	## 必须先验证（spike）
38	
39	1. Android（server）↔ macOS（client）建立 RFCOMM 通道并稳定传输 20 ms Opus 帧，测量单向延迟、抖动、吞吐。
40	2. macOS 的 TCC/沙箱是否允许非 App Store 应用打开 RFCOMM 通道；若不允许，macOS 蓝牙降级为“不可用”并在 UI 明示。
41	3. RFCOMM 流控下的帧粘包/半包处理（长度前缀 + 有界缓冲）。
42	4. 断线重连、蓝牙关闭/打开、设备休眠后的恢复。
43	5. 蓝牙与 LAN 同时可用时的优先级与回退策略。
44	
45	## Spike 记录
46	
47	- 2026-11-14：macOS 27 上 `IOBluetoothDevice.pairedDevices()` 触发蓝牙 TCC 授权弹窗；授权后成功枚举 10 台已配对设备（含 Xiaomi 15）。
48	- 2026-11-14：SDP 查询成功，可读取服务名与 RFCOMM channel ID（Xiaomi 15 的 Handsfree Gateway = 1、SMS/MMS = 26 等），证明 client 侧按 UUID 找 channel 的路径可用。
49	- 2026-11-15：端到端打通。Android `listenUsingRfcommWithServiceRecord("liino", UUID)` 发布服务；macOS SDP 查到 `liino` channel 7，`openRFCOMMChannelSync` 成功，收到 `LIINO-BT-READY`，发送 `hello` 收到 `echo:hello`。
50	- 2026-11-15 实测（Xiaomi 15 ↔ macOS，RFCOMM，1 KB 回显）：RTT min 26.0 ms / p50 36.6 ms / p95 96.1 ms；吞吐约 11.1 KB/s（单向 payload，回显双向约 190 kbps）。结论：足够 Opus 64 kbps + 20 ms 帧（约 8 KB/s），但 p95 抖动偏高，必须依赖 Jitter Buffer；最终帧格式尚未接入。
51	
52	## 代价
53	
54	- 三端各写一套平台桥，无法复用 MicYou 现成代码。
55	- 蓝牙带宽与延迟不如 Wi-Fi，音质参数需要单独调优。
56	- macOS 可能无法支持，产品需要接受平台差异。
57	
58	## 备选方案（已评估，不采用）
59	
60	- **浏览器 Web Bluetooth**：只支持 BLE GATT，访问不到 Classic 蓝牙的 RFCOMM/SPP；GATT 通知的吞吐与连接间隔延迟不适合连续音频，且 Safari/Firefox 不支持。**否决**。浏览器场景应走 MicYou 已有的 HTTP/WebSocket web 模式。
61	- **Rust `webbluetooth` crate**：不是纯浏览器绑定；它用各平台原生后端（CoreBluetooth/WinRT/BlueZ/Android）提供 Web Bluetooth 形状的 API，并提供 `classic`/`rfcomm` feature。但 `rfcomm` **只在 Linux 与 Android 实现**，macOS/Windows 仍是 BLE；浏览器 WASM 也只有 BLE。**无法替代 macOS/Windows 的 RFCOMM**。版本 0.0.2（2026-09）较新，作为 Linux/Android 的备选观察。
62	- **Qt Bluetooth FFI**：Qt 6 的 Classic Bluetooth（`QBluetoothSocket` RFCOMM）在 Android/Linux/macOS/Windows 均有后端，技术上可用。但需要把 QtCore/QtBluetooth（macOS 还需 QGuiApplication 事件循环）链入 Rust daemon，增加数十 MB 运行时、LGPLv3 合规与 C++ 构建链；macOS 后端本质上仍依赖 IOBluetooth（同样面临废弃风险）。**否决**，收益不抵成本。
63	- BLE L2CAP CoC：推迟评估。
64	- 仅 Android↔Windows 支持蓝牙，macOS 走 LAN/USB：可作为降级方案。

1	# ADR-0009：macOS 蓝牙通过独立 Swift helper 接入 daemon
2	
3	- 状态：Accepted
4	- 日期：2026-11-14（2026-11-15 依据 spike 结果修订）
5	
6	## 背景
7	
8	macOS 的 RFCOMM 只有 `IOBluetooth`（Objective-C，自 10.13 起废弃），而桌面引擎是 Rust daemon。候选方案：
9	
10	1. Rust 直接调 ObjC（`objc` crate + 手写 delegate）：无额外进程，但需要大量 unsafe。
11	2. **独立 Swift helper 进程**：隔离清楚、直接复用已验证的 Swift 代码，但多一个进程与一次管道拷贝。
12	3. Objective-C C-ABI 静态库：无额外进程，但 ObjC delegate → C 回调 → Rust 的生命周期管理复杂。
13	
14	## 决策
15	
16	采用 **方案 2：独立 Swift helper**。
17	
18	- 源码：`apps/liino_app/macos/bt_helper/main.swift`；构建：`bt_helper/build.sh`。
19	- 接口：`liino-bt-helper --address <BT MAC> [--service liino]`，把 RFCOMM 收到的字节写到 stdout，把 stdin 的字节写入 RFCOMM。**不做分帧**，分帧由 daemon 负责（与 TCP/UDP 相同的长度前缀 protobuf）。
20	- daemon 通过子进程管理：启动、按退出码重启、关闭时终止；helper 的 stderr 进入 daemon 日志。
21	- 蓝牙 TCC 授权记在宿主 App/daemon 进程；2026-11-15 实测“App bundle 启动子 helper”可以继承授权并成功枚举设备，无需为 helper 单独申请权限。
22	- 音频帧只在 daemon 与 helper 的管道间流动，不经过 Flutter。
23	
24	## 依据（spike 结果）
25	
26	- Android `listenUsingRfcommWithServiceRecord` + macOS SDP 查询 → `openRFCOMMChannelSync` 成功建立通道（channel 7）。
27	- 1 KB 回显：RTT p50 36.6 ms / p95 96.1 ms；回显吞吐约 11.1 KB/s，足够 Opus 64 kbps。
28	- 管道带宽远高于 11 KB/s，helper 进程不会成为瓶颈；额外延迟在亚毫秒级。
29	
30	## 代价
31	
32	- 多一个需要打包、签名、守护的子进程；崩溃隔离反而更好。
33	- `IOBluetooth` 已废弃，未来 macOS 可能移除；保留 LAN/USB 回退。
34	- helper 需要知道设备地址；设备发现仍由 Android 的 NSD / 桌面配对列表提供。
35	
36	## 备选方案
37	
38	- C-ABI 静态库：如果后续对延迟/进程数量有硬要求，再切换；接口可保持字节流不变。
39	- 纯 Rust ObjC：不采用。

1	//! macOS Bluetooth link over the bundled Swift helper.
2	//!
3	//! The helper owns `IOBluetooth` (ADR-0009) and bridges the RFCOMM channel to
4	//! its stdin/stdout. The daemon treats that pipe as a raw byte stream; framing
5	//! is added by the transport layer.
6	
7	use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
8	use std::io::{Read, Write};
9	use std::path::PathBuf;
10	use std::process::{Child, ChildStdin, Command, Stdio};
11	use std::thread;
12	use std::time::Duration;
13	
14	const CONNECT_GRACE: Duration = Duration::from_millis(900);
15	
16	#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
17	pub struct BtDevice {
18	    pub address: String,
19	    pub name: String,
20	}
21	
22	/// Resolves the helper: explicit override, next to the daemon (App bundle), or
23	/// the workspace build directory.
24	pub fn helper_path() -> Result<PathBuf, String> {
25	    if let Ok(path) = std::env::var("LIINO_BT_HELPER") {
26	        if !path.is_empty() {
27	            return Ok(PathBuf::from(path));
28	        }
29	    }
30	    if let Ok(executable) = std::env::current_exe() {
31	        if let Some(dir) = executable.parent() {
32	            let candidate = dir.join("liino-bt-helper");
33	            if candidate.is_file() {
34	                return Ok(candidate);
35	            }
36	        }
37	    }
38	    let dev = PathBuf::from(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"))
39	        .join("../../apps/liino_app/build/bt_helper/liino-bt-helper");
40	    if dev.is_file() {
41	        return Ok(dev);
42	    }
43	    Err("liino-bt-helper not found; set LIINO_BT_HELPER".to_string())
44	}
45	
46	pub fn list_devices() -> Result<Vec<BtDevice>, String> {
47	    let helper = helper_path()?;
48	    let output = Command::new(&helper)
49	        .arg("--list")
50	        .output()
51	        .map_err(|e| format!("run {}: {e}", helper.display()))?;
52	    if !output.status.success() {
53	        let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr);
54	        return Err(format!("bluetooth helper exited: {}", stderr.trim()));
55	    }
56	    serde_json::from_slice(&output.stdout).map_err(|e| format!("invalid helper output: {e}"))
57	}
58	
59	pub struct BluetoothLink {
60	    address: String,
61	    child: Child,
62	    stdin: ChildStdin,
63	    _reader: thread::JoinHandle<()>,
64	}
65	
66	impl BluetoothLink {
67	    pub fn connect(address: &str) -> Result<Self, String> {
68	        if address.trim().is_empty() {
69	            return Err("Bluetooth address is empty".to_string());
70	        }
71	        let helper = helper_path()?;
72	        let mut child = Command::new(&helper)
73	            .arg("--address")
74	            .arg(address)
75	            .stdin(Stdio::piped())
76	            .stdout(Stdio::piped())
77	            .stderr(Stdio::inherit())
78	            .spawn()
79	            .map_err(|e| format!("spawn {}: {e}", helper.display()))?;
80	
81	        let stdin = child
82	            .stdin
83	            .take()
84	            .ok_or_else(|| "helper stdin unavailable".to_string())?;
85	        let stdout = child
86	            .stdout
87	            .take()
88	            .ok_or_else(|| "helper stdout unavailable".to_string())?;
89	
90	        // Drain incoming bytes so a slow consumer cannot block the helper.
91	        // The transport layer will replace this with a framed channel.
92	        let reader = thread::spawn(move || {
93	            let mut reader = std::io::BufReader::new(stdout);
94	            let mut buffer = [0u8; 4096];
95	            while let Ok(read) = reader.read(&mut buffer) {
96	                if read == 0 {
97	                    break;
98	                }
99	            }
100	        });
101	
102	        thread::sleep(CONNECT_GRACE);
103	        if let Some(status) = child
104	            .try_wait()
105	            .map_err(|e| format!("helper status: {e}"))?
106	        {
107	            return Err(format!("Bluetooth helper exited early ({status})"));
108	        }
109	
110	        Ok(Self {
111	            address: address.to_string(),
112	            child,
113	            stdin,
114	            _reader: reader,
115	        })
116	    }
117	
118	    pub fn address(&self) -> &str {
119	        &self.address
120	    }
121	
122	    /// Writes raw bytes to the RFCOMM channel. Used once the framed transport
123	    /// lands; kept here so the link and the pipe stay a single unit.
124	    #[allow(dead_code)]
125	    pub fn write(&mut self, bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<(), String> {
126	        self.stdin
127	            .write_all(bytes)
128	            .and_then(|_| self.stdin.flush())
129	            .map_err(|e| format!("bluetooth write: {e}"))
130	    }
131	}
132	
133	impl Drop for BluetoothLink {
134	    fn drop(&mut self) {
135	        let _ = self.child.kill();
136	        let _ = self.child.wait();
137	    }
138	}

1	//! RFCOMM over IOBluetooth — macOS only, behind the `rfcomm` feature.
2	//!
3	//! CoreBluetooth is LE-only and always will be; Bluetooth Classic on a Mac is
4	//! a different framework, IOBluetooth, with a different idea of what a device
5	//! is. That difference is the whole shape of this module:
6	//!
7	//! * **A device is an address or a name, never a CoreBluetooth identifier** —
8	//!   see [`crate::classic`]. A dual-mode device, LE for control and Classic
9	//!   for data, is bridged by its name: [`Target::Name`](crate::classic::Target::Name).
10	//! * **Callbacks arrive on the main thread's run loop** — the open completing,
11	//!   every chunk of data, the peer closing — whichever thread opened the
12	//!   channel. So the process has to keep that run loop turning: an app does,
13	//!   with `NSApplication`; a command-line program has to call `CFRunLoopRun`
14	//!   on its main thread and do its own work on another. Where it does not,
15	//!   the open fails and says so, rather than opening a channel that never
16	//!   delivers. (This was established against a real Linux peer; the mock in
17	//!   the tests delivers on the opening thread, so it tests the pump, not this.)
18	//! * Each channel still gets a **pump**: one thread that looks the device up,
19	//!   opens the channel and does every write, so a blocking `writeSync` never
20	//!   stalls the caller or the main thread.
21	//!
22	//! The delegate is synthesised at run time like every other one in this crate.
23	//! `IOBluetoothRFCOMMChannelDelegate` is an informal protocol, so there is
24	//! nothing to declare conformance to: the channel asks the object whether it
25	//! responds to each selector and calls the ones it does.
26	//!
27	//! # What macOS asks of the process
28	//!
29	//! Opening a channel fails with `kIOReturnNotPermitted` unless the binary is
30	//! signed with the `com.apple.security.device.bluetooth` entitlement, and the
31	//! device has to be paired in System Settings first: IOBluetooth will not pair
32	//! on a channel's behalf.

57	const IO_RETURN_SUCCESS: i32 = 0;
58	/// `kIOReturnNotPermitted`, which here means the process lacks the Bluetooth
59	/// entitlement.
60	const IO_RETURN_NOT_PERMITTED: u32 = 0xe000_02bc;
61	
62	/// A name for an `IOReturn` worth recognising in an error message.
63	fn io_return_name(code: i32) -> &'static str {
64	    match code as u32 {
65	        0x0000_0000 => "kIOReturnSuccess",
66	        0xe000_02bc => "kIOReturnNotPermitted",
67	        0xe000_02be => "kIOReturnExclusiveAccess",
68	        0xe000_02c0 => "kIOReturnNotAttached",
69	        0xe000_02c7 => "kIOReturnAborted",
70	        0xe000_02d8 => "kIOReturnNotOpen",
71	        0xe000_02ed => "kIOReturnTimeout",
72	        _ => "unrecognised IOReturn",
73	    }
74	}
75	
76	fn io_error(what: &str, code: i32) -> String {
77	    let hint = if code as u32 == IO_RETURN_NOT_PERMITTED {
78	        "; the process needs the com.apple.security.device.bluetooth entitlement, which recent macOS \
79	         only honours inside a signed .app bundle"
80	    } else {
81	        ""
82	    };
83	    format!(
84	        "{what} ({}, 0x{:08x}){hint}",
85	        io_return_name(code),
86	        code as u32
87	    )
88	}

103	// ── The pump ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
104	
105	struct Pump {
106	    channel_id: u8,
107	    /// Chunks waiting to go out, front first.
108	    outgoing: Mutex<VecDeque<Vec<u8>>>,
109	    sink: Arc<dyn ChannelSink>,
110	    closed: Mutex<Option<Closed>>,
111	    stop: AtomicBool,
112	    /// The status `rfcommChannelOpenComplete:status:` reported, once it has.
113	    open_status: Mutex<Option<i32>>,
114	    /// The largest single write the channel takes.
115	    mtu: AtomicU16,
116	    /// The pump thread's runloop, so a writer can interrupt its wait.
117	    runloop: AtomicPtr<c_void>,
118	}
119	
120	impl Pump {
121	    fn finish(&self, reason: Closed) {
122	        {
123	            let mut closed = self.closed.lock().unwrap();
124	            if closed.is_some() {
125	                // Already finished; `on_closed` is called exactly once.
126	                return;
127	            }
128	            *closed = Some(reason.clone());
129	        }
130	        self.stop.store(true, Ordering::Release);
131	        self.sink.on_closed(reason);
132	    }
133	
134	    /// End the run loop's current turn, so the pump looks at its queue now.
135	    fn wake(&self) {
136	        let rl = self.runloop.load(Ordering::Acquire);
137	        if !rl.is_null() {
138	            unsafe { CFRunLoopStop(rl) };
139	        }
140	    }
141	
142	    /// Write everything queued. Pump thread only.
143	    ///
144	    /// # Safety
145	    /// `channel` must be an open `IOBluetoothRFCOMMChannel`.
146	    unsafe fn drain_output(&self, channel: Id) {
147	        let mtu = usize::from(self.mtu.load(Ordering::Acquire).max(1));
148	        loop {
149	            // Popped one at a time so the lock is not held across a write that
150	            // blocks until the controller has taken the bytes.
151	            let Some(chunk) = self.outgoing.lock().unwrap().pop_front() else {
152	                return;
153	            };
154	            for piece in chunk.chunks(mtu) {
155	                let status = unsafe {
156	                    crate::msg_send_t![
157	                        i32;
158	                        channel,
159	                        writeSync: piece.as_ptr() as *mut c_void,
160	                        length: piece.len() as u16
161	                    ]
162	                };
163	                if status != IO_RETURN_SUCCESS {
164	                    self.finish(Closed::Error(io_error("RFCOMM write failed", status)));
165	                    return;
166	                }
167	            }
168	        }
169	    }
170	}
171	
172	// ── IOBluetoothRFCOMMChannelDelegate, synthesised ───────────────────────────
173	
174	static PUMPS: OnceLock<Mutex<HashMap<usize, Arc<Pump>>>> = OnceLock::new();
175	
176	fn pumps() -> &'static Mutex<HashMap<usize, Arc<Pump>>> {
177	    PUMPS.get_or_init(|| Mutex::new(HashMap::new()))
178	}
179	
180	fn pump_for(delegate: Id) -> Option<Arc<Pump>> {
181	    pumps()
182	        .lock()
183	        .ok()
184	        .and_then(|m| m.get(&(delegate as usize)).cloned())
185	}
186	
187	static DELEGATE_CLASS: OnceLock<usize> = OnceLock::new();
188	
189	fn delegate_class() -> Id {
190	    *DELEGATE_CLASS.get_or_init(|| {
191	        for attempt in 0..64u32 {
192	            let name = if attempt == 0 {
193	                c"WBRustRFCOMMChannelDelegate".to_owned()
194	            } else {
195	                std::ffi::CString::new(format!("WBRustRFCOMMChannelDelegate{attempt}"))
196	                    .expect("class name")
197	            };
198	            let Some(builder) = (unsafe { ClassBuilder::new(c"NSObject", &name) }) else {
199	                continue;
200	            };
201	            // SAFETY: each implementation matches its encoding — an object, a
202	            // `void *` and a `size_t`; an object and an `IOReturn`; an object.
203	            return unsafe {
204	                builder
205	                    .method(
206	                        c"rfcommChannelData:data:length:",
207	                        on_data as *const c_void,
208	                        c"v@:@^vQ",
209	                    )
210	                    .method(
211	                        c"rfcommChannelOpenComplete:status:",
212	                        on_open_complete as *const c_void,
213	                        c"v@:@i",
214	                    )
215	                    .method(c"rfcommChannelClosed:", on_closed as *const c_void, c"v@:@")
216	                    .register()
217	            } as usize;
218	        }
219	        panic!("could not register an RFCOMM delegate class after 64 attempts");
220	    }) as Id
221	}
222	
223	unsafe extern "C" fn on_data(
224	    this: Id,
225	    _cmd: *const c_void,
226	    _channel: Id,
227	    data: *const u8,
228	    length: usize,
229	) {
230	    if data.is_null() || length == 0 {
231	        return;
232	    }
233	    if let Some(pump) = pump_for(this) {
234	        // The buffer is IOBluetooth's and is reused after this returns.
235	        let bytes = unsafe { core::slice::from_raw_parts(data, length) }.to_vec();
236	        pump.sink.on_bytes(bytes);
237	    }
238	}
239	
240	unsafe extern "C" fn on_open_complete(this: Id, _cmd: *const c_void, _channel: Id, status: i32) {
241	    if let Some(pump) = pump_for(this) {
242	        *pump.open_status.lock().unwrap() = Some(status);
243	    }
244	}
245	
246	unsafe extern "C" fn on_closed(this: Id, _cmd: *const c_void, _channel: Id) {
247	    if let Some(pump) = pump_for(this) {
248	        // A no-op if this side closed it: the reason is already recorded.
249	        pump.finish(Closed::ByPeer);
250	    }
251	}

255	/// An open RFCOMM byte stream.
256	///
257	/// Dropping this closes the channel and stops its pump thread.
258	pub struct Channel {
259	    channel: u8,
260	    peer: String,
261	    pump: Arc<Pump>,
262	}
263	
264	impl Channel {
265	    /// The RFCOMM server channel number.
266	    pub fn channel(&self) -> u8 {
267	        self.channel
268	    }
269	
270	    /// The peer's Bluetooth address.
271	    pub fn peer_id(&self) -> &str {
272	        &self.peer
273	    }
274	
275	    /// Queue bytes for sending.
276	    ///
277	    /// Returns once the bytes are queued, not once they are on the air.
278	    pub fn send(&self, bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<(), Closed> {
279	        if let Some(reason) = self.closed() {
280	            return Err(reason);
281	        }
282	        if bytes.is_empty() {
283	            return Ok(());
284	        }
285	        self.pump.outgoing.lock().unwrap().push_back(bytes.to_vec());
286	        self.pump.wake();
287	        Ok(())
288	    }
289	
290	    /// How many queued bytes have not yet been written.
291	    pub fn pending_bytes(&self) -> usize {
292	        self.pump
293	            .outgoing
294	            .lock()
295	            .unwrap()
296	            .iter()
297	            .map(Vec::len)
298	            .sum()
299	    }
300	
301	    /// Why the stream closed, or `None` while it is open.
302	    pub fn closed(&self) -> Option<Closed> {
303	        self.pump.closed.lock().unwrap().clone()
304	    }
305	
306	    /// Close the stream.
307	    pub fn close(&self) {
308	        self.pump.finish(Closed::Locally);
309	        self.pump.wake();
310	    }
311	}
312

365	    /// Handed in ready-made: the seam the mock device in the tests uses.
366	    #[cfg(test)]
367	    Device(Retained),
368	}
369	
370	/// One thread per channel: opens it, runs the runloop, does all I/O.
371	fn spawn_pump(pump: Arc<Pump>, source: Source, opened: Opened) -> std::io::Result<()> {
372	    std::thread::Builder::new()
373	        .name(format!("webbluetooth-rfcomm-{}", pump.channel_id))
374	        .spawn(move || {
375	            let _pool = objc::AutoreleasePool::new();
376	            unsafe { run_pump(&pump, source, opened) };
377	            pump.runloop.store(std::ptr::null_mut(), Ordering::Release);
378	        })
379	        .map(|_| ())
380	}
381	
382	/// # Safety
383	/// Must run on a thread of its own, inside an autorelease pool.
384	unsafe fn run_pump(pump: &Arc<Pump>, source: Source, opened: Opened) {
385	    let fail = |opened: Opened, message: String| {
386	        pump.finish(Closed::Error(message.clone()));
387	        let _ = opened.send(Err(message));
388	    };
389	
390	    let found = match source {
391	        Source::Target(target) => unsafe { find_device(&target) },
392	        #[cfg(test)]
393	        Source::Device(device) => Ok(device),
394	    };
395	    let device = match found {
396	        Ok(device) => device,
397	        Err(message) => return fail(opened, message),
398	    };
399	
400	    // A delegate object per channel, so the callbacks can find this pump.
401	    let delegate = unsafe {
402	        let obj: Id = crate::msg_send![delegate_class(), alloc];
403	        let obj: Id = crate::msg_send![obj, init];
404	        match Retained::adopt(obj) {
405	            Some(delegate) => delegate,
406	            None => return fail(opened, "could not create the RFCOMM delegate".into()),
407	        }
408	    };
409	    pumps().lock().unwrap().insert(delegate.key(), pump.clone());
410	
411	    // A run loop with no input source returns at once instead of waiting, so
412	    // it is given a port to hold it open. IOBluetooth adds its own sources
413	    // when the channel opens; this covers the time before it has.
414	    let (run_loop, mode, port) = unsafe {
415	        let run_loop: Id = crate::msg_send![require_class(c"NSRunLoop"), currentRunLoop];
416	        let mode = global_nsstring(c"NSDefaultRunLoopMode");
417	        let port: Id = crate::msg_send![require_class(c"NSMachPort"), port];
418	        if !run_loop.is_null() && !mode.is_null() && !port.is_null() {
419	            crate::msg_send_void![run_loop, addPort: port, forMode: mode];
420	        }
421	        (run_loop, mode, Retained::retain(port))
422	    };
423	    pump.runloop
424	        .store(unsafe { CFRunLoopGetCurrent() }, Ordering::Release);
425	
426	    let channel = unsafe { open_channel(pump, &device, &delegate, opened) };
427	    if let Some(channel) = &channel {
428	        unsafe {
429	            while !pump.stop.load(Ordering::Acquire) {
430	                // Returns when a source fires, when `wake` stops it, or after
431	                // one tick — whichever is first.
432	                CFRunLoopRunInMode(kCFRunLoopDefaultMode, TICK_SECONDS, true);
433	                if pump.stop.load(Ordering::Acquire) {
434	                    break;
435	                }
436	                pump.drain_output(channel.as_ptr());
437	                if !crate::msg_send_t![bool; channel.as_ptr(), isOpen] {
438	                    pump.finish(Closed::ByPeer);
439	                }
440	            }
441	            // Detached first, so closing does not call back into a pump that
442	            // is about to be forgotten.
443	            crate::msg_send_void![channel.as_ptr(), setDelegate: NIL];
444	            let _: i32 = crate::msg_send_t![i32; channel.as_ptr(), closeChannel];
445	        }
446	    }
447	
448	    pumps().lock().unwrap().remove(&delegate.key());
449	    if let Some(port) = port {
450	        if !run_loop.is_null() && !mode.is_null() {
451	            unsafe { crate::msg_send_void![run_loop, removePort: port.as_ptr(), forMode: mode] };
452	        }
453	    }
454	}
455	
456	/// Open the channel and wait for the delegate to say it is up.
457	///
458	/// Resolves `opened` either way. `None` means the pump has nothing to run.
459	///
460	/// # Safety
461	/// Pump thread only; `device` must be an `IOBluetoothDevice`.
462	unsafe fn open_channel(
463	    pump: &Arc<Pump>,
464	    device: &Retained,
465	    delegate: &Retained,
466	    opened: Opened,
467	) -> Option<Retained> {
468	    let fail = |opened: Opened, message: String| -> Option<Retained> {
469	        pump.finish(Closed::Error(message.clone()));
470	        let _ = opened.send(Err(message));
471	        None
472	    };
473	
474	    unsafe {
475	        // The channel open brings the baseband link up itself, but doing it
476	        // first separates "the device is not there" from "the device refused
477	        // the channel". Its result is not fatal: the open below reports.
478	        if !crate::msg_send_t![bool; device.as_ptr(), isConnected] {
479	            let _: i32 = crate::msg_send_t![i32; device.as_ptr(), openConnection];
480	        }
481	
482	        // The asynchronous open, deliberately. The synchronous one returns an
483	        // open channel whose delegate is never called with data.
484	        let mut raw: Id = NIL;
485	        let status = crate::msg_send_t![
486	            i32;
487	            device.as_ptr(),
488	            openRFCOMMChannelAsync: &mut raw as *mut Id,
489	            withChannelID: pump.channel_id,
490	            delegate: delegate.as_ptr()
491	        ];
492	        if status != IO_RETURN_SUCCESS {
493	            let what = format!("could not open RFCOMM channel {}", pump.channel_id);
494	            return fail(opened, io_error(&what, status));
495	        }
496	        // Returned unowned; held for as long as the pump runs.
497	        let Some(channel) = Retained::retain(raw) else {
498	            return fail(opened, "IOBluetooth returned no RFCOMM channel".into());
499	        };
500	
501	        let deadline = Instant::now() + OPEN_TIMEOUT;
502	        loop {
503	            if CFRunLoopRunInMode(kCFRunLoopDefaultMode, TICK_SECONDS, true) == RUN_FINISHED {
504	                // No sources at all: do not spin while waiting.
505	                std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(10));
506	            }
507	            // The open status first: a peer that opens, sends and hangs up at
508	            // once delivers all three in one turn, and its data is still owed
509	            // to the caller — on a channel that is already closed.
510	            let status = *pump.open_status.lock().unwrap();
511	            match status {
512	                Some(IO_RETURN_SUCCESS) => break,
513	                Some(status) => {
514	                    let what = format!("RFCOMM channel {} did not open", pump.channel_id);
515	                    return fail(opened, io_error(&what, status));
516	                }
517	                None => {}
518	            }
519	            // Nobody is waiting for the channel any more, or it closed before
520	            // it finished opening.
521	            if opened.is_canceled() || pump.stop.load(Ordering::Acquire) {
522	                pump.finish(Closed::Locally);
523	                crate::msg_send_void![channel.as_ptr(), setDelegate: NIL];
524	                let _: i32 = crate::msg_send_t![i32; channel.as_ptr(), closeChannel];
525	                let reason = pump.closed.lock().unwrap().clone();
526	                let _ = opened.send(Err(format!(
527	                    "RFCOMM channel {} closed before it opened: {reason:?}",
528	                    pump.channel_id
529	                )));
530	                return None;
531	            }
532	            // `isOpen` alone is not enough. IOBluetooth delivers every
533	            // delegate callback — this one, and all incoming data — on the
534	            // main thread's run loop, and a channel that opens in a process
535	            // whose main run loop is not turning would deliver nothing
536	            // after it. Waiting for the callback is what finds that out.
537	            if Instant::now() >= deadline {
538	                let opened_anyway = crate::msg_send_t![bool; channel.as_ptr(), isOpen];
539	                let _: i32 = crate::msg_send_t![i32; channel.as_ptr(), closeChannel];
540	                let message = if opened_anyway {
541	                    format!(
542	                        "RFCOMM channel {} opened, but IOBluetooth never called back: it \
543	                         delivers RFCOMM events on the main thread's run loop, which is not \
544	                         running in this process. An app's is; a command-line program has to \
545	                         turn it (CFRunLoopRun on the main thread) and do its work elsewhere",
546	                        pump.channel_id
547	                    )
548	                } else {
549	                    format!(
550	                        "RFCOMM channel {} did not open within {} s",
551	                        pump.channel_id,
552	                        OPEN_TIMEOUT.as_secs()
553	                    )
554	                };
555	                return fail(opened, message);
556	            }
557	        }
558	
559	        let mtu = crate::msg_send_t![u16; channel.as_ptr(), getMTU];
560	        pump.mtu
561	            .store(if mtu == 0 { FALLBACK_MTU } else { mtu }, Ordering::Release);
562	
563	        let peer = device_address(device.as_ptr()).unwrap_or_default();
564	        if opened.send(Ok(peer)).is_err() {
565	            // The caller gave up in the instant before the answer.
566	            pump.finish(Closed::Locally);
567	        }
568	        Some(channel)
569	    }
570	}
571	
572	/// `kCFRunLoopRunFinished`: the run loop had no sources or timers to wait on.
573	const RUN_FINISHED: i32 = 1;
574	
575	/// Open an RFCOMM stream to `target` on a server channel.
576	///
577	/// Resolves once the channel is open. The device must already be paired.
578	pub async fn open(target: Target, channel: u8) -> webbluetooth_core::Result<RfcommChannel> {
579	    open_source(Source::Target(target), channel).await
580	}
581	
582	async fn open_source(source: Source, channel: u8) -> webbluetooth_core::Result<RfcommChannel> {
583	    use webbluetooth_core::Error;
584	
585	    if !(1..=30).contains(&channel) {
586	        return Err(Error::InvalidModification(
587	            "RFCOMM channel must be between 1 and 30".into(),
588	        ));
589	    }
590	
591	    let (channel_sink, sink, incoming) = webbluetooth_core::l2cap::sink();
592	    let pump = Arc::new(Pump {
593	        channel_id: channel,
594	        outgoing: Mutex::new(VecDeque::new()),
595	        sink: channel_sink,
596	        closed: Mutex::new(None),
597	        stop: AtomicBool::new(false),
598	        open_status: Mutex::new(None),
599	        mtu: AtomicU16::new(FALLBACK_MTU),
600	        runloop: AtomicPtr::new(std::ptr::null_mut()),
601	    });
602	
603	    let (opened_tx, opened_rx) = oneshot::channel();
604	    spawn_pump(pump.clone(), source, opened_tx)
605	        .map_err(|error| Error::Network(format!("could not start the RFCOMM pump: {error}")))?;
606	
607	    match opened_rx.await {
608	        Ok(Ok(peer)) => Ok(RfcommChannel::new(
609	            Channel {
610	                channel,
611	                peer,
612	                pump,
613	            },
614	            sink,
615	            incoming,
616	        )),
617	        Ok(Err(message)) => Err(Error::Network(message)),
618	        Err(_) => Err(Error::Aborted(
619	            "the RFCOMM pump stopped before opening".into(),
620	        )),
621	    }
622	}

1	//! Open an RFCOMM channel to a paired Bluetooth Classic device, on macOS.
2	//!
3	//! ```sh
4	//! # List what is paired.
5	//! cargo run -p webbluetooth --example rfcomm_macos --features rfcomm
6	//! # Open channel 1 on one of them, by address or by name.
7	//! cargo run -p webbluetooth --example rfcomm_macos --features rfcomm -- AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF 1
8	//! cargo run -p webbluetooth --example rfcomm_macos --features rfcomm -- "Some Headset" 1
9	//! ```
10	//!
11	//! Not part of Web Bluetooth, and not CoreBluetooth either: Bluetooth Classic
12	//! on a Mac is IOBluetooth, which the `rfcomm` feature links. The device has to
13	//! be paired in System Settings beforehand.
14	//!
15	//! **Events arrive on the main thread's run loop**, so `main` keeps it turning
16	//! and the work runs on another thread — see `main` below.
17	//!
18	//! **Opening needs an entitlement.** macOS refuses an RFCOMM channel with
19	//! `kIOReturnNotPermitted` unless the binary is signed with
20	//! `com.apple.security.device.bluetooth`, which a bare `cargo run` binary is
21	//! not. Listing the paired devices works without it.
22	
23	#[cfg(not(all(feature = "rfcomm", target_os = "macos")))]
24	fn main() {
25	    eprintln!("macOS only, and it needs --features rfcomm.");
26	    std::process::exit(1);
27	}
28	
29	/// IOBluetooth delivers every RFCOMM event — the open completing, each chunk of
30	/// data, the peer closing — on the main thread's run loop. So the work runs on
31	/// another thread and the main thread keeps that run loop turning until it is
32	/// done. An app gets this from `NSApplication`; a command-line program has to
33	/// do it itself, and without it the open fails and says so.
34	#[cfg(all(feature = "rfcomm", target_os = "macos"))]
35	fn main() -> webbluetooth::Result<()> {
36	    use std::sync::mpsc;
37	    use std::time::Duration;
38	
39	    unsafe extern "C" {
40	        fn CFRunLoopRunInMode(mode: *const std::ffi::c_void, seconds: f64, ret: bool) -> i32;
41	        static kCFRunLoopDefaultMode: *const std::ffi::c_void;
42	    }
43	
44	    let (done_tx, done) = mpsc::channel();
45	    std::thread::spawn(move || {
46	        let _ = done_tx.send(futures_executor::block_on(run()));
47	    });
48	    loop {
49	        match done.recv_timeout(Duration::ZERO) {
50	            Ok(result) => return result,
51	            Err(mpsc::RecvTimeoutError::Disconnected) => return Ok(()),
52	            Err(mpsc::RecvTimeoutError::Timeout) => {}
53	        }
54	        unsafe { CFRunLoopRunInMode(kCFRunLoopDefaultMode, 0.1, false) };
55	    }
56	}
57	
58	#[cfg(all(feature = "rfcomm", target_os = "macos"))]
59	async fn run() -> webbluetooth::Result<()> {
60	    use webbluetooth::stream::StreamExt;
61	    use webbluetooth::Bluetooth;
62	
63	    let bluetooth = Bluetooth::shared();
64	    let paired = bluetooth.paired_classic_devices().await?;
65	
66	    let mut args = std::env::args().skip(1);
67	    let Some(wanted) = args.next() else {
68	        println!("{} paired Bluetooth Classic device(s):", paired.len());
69	        for device in &paired {
70	            println!(
71	                "  {}  {}{}",
72	                device
73	                    .address
74	                    .map(|a| a.to_string())
75	                    .unwrap_or_else(|| "(no address)".into()),
76	                device.name.as_deref().unwrap_or("(unnamed)"),
77	                if device.connected {
78	                    "  [connected]"
79	                } else {
80	                    ""
81	                },
82	            );
83	        }
84	        return Ok(());
85	    };
86	    let channel: u8 = match args.next() {
87	        Some(arg) => arg
88	            .parse()
89	            .unwrap_or_else(|_| panic!("not a channel: {arg}")),
90	        None => 1,
91	    };
92	
93	    // A name is resolved to its address here, so the open itself is by
94	    // address and cannot land on a different device of the same name.
95	    let address = paired
96	        .iter()
97	        .find(|device| device.name.as_deref() == Some(wanted.as_str()))
98	        .and_then(|device| device.address)
99	        .map(|a| a.to_string())
100	        .unwrap_or(wanted);
101	
102	    println!("opening RFCOMM channel {channel} on {address}…");
103	    let rfcomm = bluetooth.open_rfcomm_channel(&address, channel).await?;
104	    println!("open. Ctrl-C to stop.");
105	
106	    let mut incoming = rfcomm.take_incoming().expect("first take");
107	    while let Some(bytes) = incoming.next().await {
108	        let hex: Vec<String> = bytes.iter().take(32).map(|b| format!("{b:02x}")).collect();
109	        println!("{:>4} B  {}", bytes.len(), hex.join(" "));
110	    }
111	    println!("closed: {:?}", rfcomm.closed());
112	    Ok(())
113	}

41	That is the whole dependency list for the example above. `webbluetooth::prelude`
42	re-exports `StreamExt`, because notifications, advertisements and disconnects
43	are all streams and a stream has no `.next()` without it — so the example used
44	to need a `futures-util` dependency nobody had mentioned.
45	
46	You do need an executor to run any of it. This crate brings none, so that it
47	works with whichever you already have; the examples use `futures_executor`,
48	which is the smallest thing that will do.
49	
50	No Swift, no Objective-C, no Java, no `libdbus`, no code generation, no shim.
51	Each platform is reached through its own C ABI directly, and where one demands
52	a type that does not exist — a CoreBluetooth delegate, an Android callback
53	subclass — it is built at run time rather than shipped.
54	
55	## Start here
56	
57	```sh
58	cargo run --example doctor    # why Bluetooth is or isn't usable
59	cargo run --example scan      # list everything in range
60	cargo run --example battery   # read the nearest battery level
61	```
62	
63	Run `doctor` first. Almost every "it finds nothing" report is an authorization
64	problem rather than anything to do with the radio — on Apple platforms a
65	process with no `NSBluetoothAlwaysUsageDescription` is reported
66	`Unauthorized` and is **never prompted**. The repository's README explains what
67	to do about that; it is the single most common way to lose an afternoon here.
68	
69	## Platforms
70	
71	| Platform | Central | Peripheral | L2CAP |
72	|---|:--:|:--:|:--:|
73	| macOS, iOS, Mac Catalyst | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
74	| tvOS, watchOS, visionOS | ✅ | ❌ | ✅ |
75	| Linux (BlueZ, or a raw socket with `linux-hci`) | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
76	| Android (API 26+) | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ (29+) |
77	| Windows 10 1709+ | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ |
78	| Browser (WebAssembly) | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ |
79	| Node.js / Deno | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ |
80	
81	`PERIPHERAL_ROLE` and `L2CAP` are `const bool`s to branch on, and the modules
82	they describe do not exist where they are `false`.
83	
84	## Native extensions
85	
86	The standard-shaped API is available from the root crate. Native extensions
87	are opt-in through Cargo features:
88	
89	| Feature | Provides |
90	|---|---|
91	| `public` | The Web Bluetooth-compatible imports under `webbluetooth::public`. |
92	| `classic` | Enables Bluetooth Classic capability reporting. |
93	| `rfcomm` | Enables RFCOMM byte streams on Linux, Android, Windows and macOS; it implies `classic`, and on macOS `apple-classic`. |
94	| `apple-classic` | macOS: Bluetooth Classic through IOBluetooth — paired-device listing; `rfcomm` turns it on. |
95	| `classic-l2cap` | Enables Bluetooth Classic L2CAP channels; it implies `classic` and is currently implemented on Linux. |
96	| `linux-hci` | Uses the Linux controller directly instead of BlueZ. |
97	| `uuid` | Converts to and from the `uuid` crate's `Uuid`. |
98	
99	For example:
100	
101	```toml
102	[dependencies]
103	webbluetooth = { version = "0.0.4", features = ["public", "rfcomm"] }
104	```
105	
106	`BluetoothDevice::mtu()` reports the negotiated ATT MTU. On Android,
107	`BluetoothDevice::request_mtu()` asks the platform to negotiate a requested
108	value; platforms that hide or automatically manage the exchange return
109	`Error::NotSupported`.
110	
111	Descriptors support `read_value()` and `write_value()` as well as
112	`read_value_at_offset()` and `write_value_at_offset()`. The offset helpers use
113	portable whole-value reads and writes, validate offsets, and enforce the
114	512-byte ATT attribute limit.
115	
116	On Linux, `BluetoothDevice::open_rfcomm_channel(channel)` opens a Bluetooth
117	Classic RFCOMM byte stream and `open_classic_l2cap_channel(psm)` opens a
118	Classic L2CAP channel. On Android, `open_rfcomm_service(service_uuid)` opens
119	an RFCOMM service-record connection. On Windows, `open_rfcomm_channel(channel)`
120	goes through WinSock. On macOS, RFCOMM is IOBluetooth's rather than
121	CoreBluetooth's, and the two share no identifier: `Bluetooth::open_rfcomm_channel(address,
122	channel)` opens by address (`Bluetooth::paired_classic_devices()` lists them),
123	and `BluetoothDevice::open_rfcomm_channel(channel)` finds a dual-mode device's
124	Classic side by name. IOBluetooth delivers RFCOMM events on the main thread's
125	run loop, so a command-line program has to keep it turning — see the
126	`rfcomm_macos` example. These transports are separate from BLE L2CAP and from the
127	Web Bluetooth surface; iOS and browser targets do not expose them.
128	
129	## What is different from a browser
130	
131	**The chooser is yours.** `requestDevice()` is defined around a user gesture
132	and a picker dialog. A library has no chrome to draw, so it is a trait:
133	`FirstMatch` (the default, and a deliberate removal of the consent step),
134	`StrongestSignal`, `TerminalChooser`, a predicate, or your own.
135	
136	**Everything else about the security model is kept** — the GATT blocklist, the
137	manufacturer-data blocklist, and the rule that a device grants access only to
138	the services that were asked for.
139	
140	## Features
141	
142	| | |
143	|---|---|
144	| `public` | Re-export the Web Bluetooth-compatible API under `webbluetooth::public`. |
145	| `classic` | Enable Bluetooth Classic capability reporting and native extensions. |
146	| `rfcomm` | Enable RFCOMM byte streams on Linux, Android, Windows and macOS; implies `classic`. |
147	| `linux-hci` | Talk to the controller directly instead of going through BlueZ. |
148	| `terminal-chooser` | A device chooser that prints numbered candidates and reads a line. |
149	| `uuid` | Convert to and from the `uuid` crate's `Uuid`. |
150	
151	## More
152	
153	The [repository](https://github.com/eugenehp/webbluetooth) has the full guide:
154	authorization, the peripheral role, L2CAP channels, state restoration, how each
155	backend works, and what is tested where. `PLATFORMS.md` is the per-platform
156	reference.
157

1	//! Bluetooth Classic devices through IOBluetooth — macOS only, behind the
2	//! `apple-classic` feature.
3	//!
4	//! CoreBluetooth is LE-only and always will be; Bluetooth Classic on a Mac is
5	//! a different framework, IOBluetooth, with a different idea of what a device
6	//! is. CoreBluetooth hides the address behind a per-host UUID and IOBluetooth
7	//! knows nothing about that UUID, so there is no way to get from a
8	//! `CBPeripheral` to its `IOBluetoothDevice` except through something both
9	//! frameworks report. [`Target`](crate::classic::Target) is those two things: an address, or — for a
10	//! dual-mode device found over LE — its name.
11	//!
12	//! This module finds devices. What is opened on them lives beside it:
13	//! [`crate::rfcomm`], behind the `rfcomm` feature.
14	
15	use crate::objc::{self, Id, Retained};
16	
17	pub use webbluetooth_core::classic::ClassicDevice;
18	
19	/// Which Bluetooth Classic device to open a channel on.
20	#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
21	pub enum Target {
22	    /// A Bluetooth address: `AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF`, or with `-` as IOBluetooth
23	    /// itself writes it.
24	    Address(String),
25	    /// The name of a paired or recently used device, matched exactly.
26	    ///
27	    /// The only bridge from a CoreBluetooth peripheral, whose address is
28	    /// hidden, to the same physical device seen through IOBluetooth.
29	    Name(String),
30	}
31	
32	/// Six bytes from `AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF` or `aa-bb-cc-dd-ee-ff`.
33	pub(crate) fn parse_address(address: &str) -> Option<[u8; 6]> {
34	    let mut bytes = [0u8; 6];
35	    let mut parts = address.split([':', '-']);
36	    for byte in &mut bytes {
37	        let part = parts.next()?;
38	        if part.len() != 2 {
39	            return None;
40	        }
41	        *byte = u8::from_str_radix(part, 16).ok()?;
42	    }
43	    parts.next().is_none().then_some(bytes)
44	}
45	
46	/// The form the rest of this workspace uses: `AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF`.
47	pub(crate) fn format_address(bytes: &[u8; 6]) -> String {
48	    bytes
49	        .iter()
50	        .map(|b| format!("{b:02X}"))
51	        .collect::<Vec<_>>()
52	        .join(":")
53	}
54	
55	// ── IOBluetoothDevice ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
56	
57	pub(crate) fn device_class() -> Result<Id, String> {
58	    let class = objc::class(c"IOBluetoothDevice");
59	    if class.is_null() {
60	        return Err("IOBluetooth is not loaded in this process".into());
61	    }
62	    Ok(class)
63	}
64	
65	/// # Safety
66	/// `device` must be an `IOBluetoothDevice`.
67	unsafe fn device_name(device: Id) -> Option<String> {
68	    unsafe { objc::to_string(crate::msg_send![device, name]) }
69	}
70	
71	/// # Safety
72	/// `device` must be an `IOBluetoothDevice`.
73	pub(crate) unsafe fn device_address(device: Id) -> Option<String> {
74	    let raw = unsafe { objc::to_string(crate::msg_send![device, addressString]) }?;
75	    parse_address(&raw).map(|bytes| format_address(&bytes))
76	}
77	
78	// Only RFCOMM opens channels on a device today; listing does not need this.
79	#[cfg_attr(not(feature = "rfcomm"), allow(dead_code))]
80	/// The devices IOBluetooth knows without an inquiry: everything paired, then
81	/// whatever was used recently.
82	///
83	/// # Safety
84	/// Must run inside an autorelease pool.
85	unsafe fn known_devices(class: Id) -> Vec<Retained> {
86	    unsafe {
87	        let mut devices = Vec::new();
88	        let paired: Id = crate::msg_send![class, pairedDevices];
89	        devices.extend(objc::array_map(paired, |d| Retained::retain(d)));
90	        let recent: Id = crate::msg_send![class, recentDevices: 10usize];
91	        devices.extend(objc::array_map(recent, |d| Retained::retain(d)));
92	        devices.into_iter().flatten().collect()
93	    }
94	}
95	
96	// Only RFCOMM opens channels on a device today; listing does not need this.
97	#[cfg_attr(not(feature = "rfcomm"), allow(dead_code))]
98	/// # Safety
99	/// Must run inside an autorelease pool.
100	pub(crate) unsafe fn find_device(target: &Target) -> Result<Retained, String> {
101	    let class = device_class()?;
102	    match target {
103	        Target::Address(address) => {
104	            let bytes = parse_address(address)
105	                .ok_or_else(|| format!("{address:?} is not a Bluetooth address"))?;
106	            // IOBluetooth writes addresses with dashes and reads them back the
107	            // same way.
108	            let dashed = format_address(&bytes).replace(':', "-");
109	            unsafe {
110	                let string = Retained::adopt(objc::nsstring(&dashed))
111	                    .ok_or_else(|| "could not build an address string".to_owned())?;
112	                let device: Id = crate::msg_send![class, deviceWithAddressString: string.as_ptr()];
113	                Retained::retain(device)
114	                    .ok_or_else(|| format!("IOBluetooth knows no device at {address}"))
115	            }
116	        }
117	        Target::Name(name) => unsafe { known_devices(class) }
118	            .into_iter()
119	            .find(|device| unsafe { device_name(device.as_ptr()) }.as_deref() == Some(name))
120	            .ok_or_else(|| {
121	                format!(
122	                    "no paired or recently used Bluetooth Classic device is named {name:?}; \
123	                     pair it in System Settings first"
124	                )
125	            }),
126	    }
127	}
128	
129	/// Every paired Bluetooth Classic device.
130	///
131	/// Answered from what the system already knows: no inquiry is run, so this
132	/// returns at once and lists devices whether or not they are in range.
133	pub fn paired_devices() -> webbluetooth_core::Result<Vec<ClassicDevice>> {
134	    let _pool = objc::AutoreleasePool::new();
135	    let class = device_class().map_err(webbluetooth_core::Error::NotSupported)?;
136	    Ok(unsafe {
137	        let paired: Id = crate::msg_send![class, pairedDevices];
138	        objc::array_map(paired, |device| ClassicDevice {
139	            address: device_address(device).and_then(|a| a.parse().ok()),
140	            name: device_name(device),
141	            class_of_device: None,
142	            bonded: true,
143	            authenticated: false,
144	            connected: crate::msg_send_t![bool; device, isConnected],
145	        })
146	    })
147	}

155	        let bytes = [0xAA, 0xBB, 0xCC, 0x0D, 0xEE, 0xFF];
156	        assert_eq!(parse_address("AA:BB:CC:0D:EE:FF"), Some(bytes));
157	        // The form `addressString` returns.

161	        assert_eq!(parse_address("AA:BB:CC:DD:EE"), None);
162	        assert_eq!(parse_address("AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF:00"), None);
163	        assert_eq!(parse_address("AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:GG"), None);
164	        assert_eq!(parse_address("A:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF"), None);
165	        // A CoreBluetooth identifier, which is what a caller is most likely to

1	//! Windows Bluetooth Classic RFCOMM over Winsock `AF_BTH`.
2	
3	#![cfg(windows)]
4	
5	use futures_channel::mpsc;
6	use futures_core::Stream;
7	use std::io::{Read, Write};
8	use std::net::Shutdown;
9	use std::os::windows::io::{FromRawSocket, RawSocket};
10	use std::pin::Pin;
11	use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, Ordering};
12	use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};
13	use webbluetooth_core::l2cap::{ChannelSink, Closed};
14	
15	const AF_BTH: i32 = 32;
16	const BTPROTO_RFCOMM: i32 = 3;
17	
18	#[repr(C)]
19	struct SockAddrBth {
20	    address_family: u16,
21	    bt_addr: u64,
22	    service_class_id: windows_sys::core::GUID,
23	    port: u32,
24	}
25	
26	/// An open Windows RFCOMM byte stream.
27	pub struct Channel {
28	    socket: Arc<std::net::TcpStream>,
29	    channel: u8,
30	    peer: String,
31	    closed: Mutex<Option<Closed>>,
32	    stopped: Arc<AtomicBool>,
33	    writing: Mutex<()>,
34	}
35	
36	impl Channel {
37	    /// Connect to a Bluetooth address and RFCOMM server channel.
38	    pub fn connect(address: &str, channel: u8, sink: Arc<dyn ChannelSink>) -> Result<Self, String> {
39	        Self::connect_inner(address, channel, unsafe { std::mem::zeroed() }, sink)
40	    }
41	
42	    /// Connect to a Classic profile by its SDP service UUID.
43	    pub fn connect_service(
44	        address: &str,
45	        service_uuid: &str,
46	        sink: Arc<dyn ChannelSink>,
47	    ) -> Result<Self, String> {
48	        Self::connect_inner(address, 0, parse_guid(service_uuid)?, sink)
49	    }
50	
51	    fn connect_inner(
52	        address: &str,
53	        channel: u8,
54	        service_class_id: windows_sys::core::GUID,
55	        sink: Arc<dyn ChannelSink>,
56	    ) -> Result<Self, String> {
57	        let bt_addr = parse_address(address)?;
58	        let has_service_uuid = service_class_id.data1 != 0
59	            || service_class_id.data2 != 0
60	            || service_class_id.data3 != 0
61	            || service_class_id.data4 != [0; 8];
62	        if !has_service_uuid && !(1..=30).contains(&channel) {
63	            return Err("RFCOMM channel must be between 1 and 30".into());
64	        }
65	        let raw = unsafe {
66	            windows_sys::Win32::Networking::WinSock::socket(
67	                AF_BTH,
68	                windows_sys::Win32::Networking::WinSock::SOCK_STREAM,
69	                BTPROTO_RFCOMM,
70	            )
71	        };
72	        if raw == windows_sys::Win32::Networking::WinSock::INVALID_SOCKET {
73	            return Err(format!("could not create RFCOMM socket: {}", last_error()));
74	        }
75	        let socket = unsafe { std::net::TcpStream::from_raw_socket(raw as RawSocket) };
76	        let address = SockAddrBth {
77	            address_family: AF_BTH as u16,
78	            bt_addr,
79	            service_class_id,
80	            port: channel as u32,
81	        };
82	        let connected = unsafe {
83	            windows_sys::Win32::Networking::WinSock::connect(
84	                raw,
85	                (&raw const address).cast(),
86	                std::mem::size_of_val(&address) as i32,
87	            )
88	        };
89	        if connected == windows_sys::Win32::Networking::WinSock::SOCKET_ERROR {
90	            return Err(format!("could not connect RFCOMM socket: {}", last_error()));
91	        }
92	        let socket = Arc::new(socket);
93	        let stopped = Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false));
94	        spawn_reader(socket.clone(), sink, stopped.clone(), channel);
95	        Ok(Self {
96	            socket,
97	            channel,
98	            peer: address_to_string(bt_addr),
99	            closed: Mutex::new(None),
100	            stopped,
101	            writing: Mutex::new(()),
102	        })
103	    }
104	
105	    pub fn channel(&self) -> u8 {
106	        self.channel
107	    }
108	    pub fn peer_id(&self) -> &str {
109	        &self.peer
110	    }
111	    pub fn send(&self, bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<(), Closed> {
112	        let _guard = self.writing.lock().unwrap();
113	        if let Some(reason) = self.closed() {
114	            return Err(reason);
115	        }
116	        let mut socket = &*self.socket;
117	        socket.write_all(bytes).map_err(|error| {
118	            let reason = Closed::Error(error.to_string());
119	            *self.closed.lock().unwrap() = Some(reason.clone());
120	            reason
121	        })
122	    }
123	    pub fn pending_bytes(&self) -> usize {
124	        0
125	    }
126	    pub fn closed(&self) -> Option<Closed> {
127	        self.closed.lock().unwrap().clone()
128	    }
129	    pub fn close(&self) {
130	        if self.closed().is_none() {
131	            *self.closed.lock().unwrap() = Some(Closed::Locally);
132	        }
133	        self.stopped.store(true, Ordering::Release);
134	        let _ = self.socket.shutdown(Shutdown::Both);
135	    }
136	}
137	
138	impl Drop for Channel {
139	    fn drop(&mut self) {
140	        self.close();
141	    }
142	}
143	
144	fn spawn_reader(
145	    socket: Arc<std::net::TcpStream>,
146	    sink: Arc<dyn ChannelSink>,
147	    stopped: Arc<AtomicBool>,
148	    channel: u8,
149	) {
150	    std::thread::Builder::new()
151	        .name(format!("webbluetooth-windows-rfcomm-{channel}"))
152	        .spawn(move || {
153	            let mut socket = &*socket;
154	            let mut bytes = [0; 4096];
155	            let reason = loop {
156	                if stopped.load(Ordering::Acquire) {
157	                    break Closed::Locally;
158	                }
159	                match socket.read(&mut bytes) {
160	                    Ok(0) => break Closed::ByPeer,
161	                    Ok(size) => sink.on_bytes(bytes[..size].to_vec()),
162	                    Err(error) => break Closed::Error(error.to_string()),
163	                }
164	            };
165	            sink.on_closed(reason);
166	        })
167	        .expect("could not start the Windows RFCOMM reader");
168	}

231	/// Listen for incoming RFCOMM connections on a server channel.
232	pub fn listen(channel: u8) -> webbluetooth_core::Result<RfcommListener> {
233	    if !(1..=30).contains(&channel) {
234	        return Err(webbluetooth_core::Error::InvalidModification(
235	            "RFCOMM channel must be between 1 and 30".into(),
236	        ));
237	    }
238	    let raw = unsafe {
239	        windows_sys::Win32::Networking::WinSock::socket(
240	            AF_BTH,
241	            windows_sys::Win32::Networking::WinSock::SOCK_STREAM,
242	            BTPROTO_RFCOMM,
243	        )
244	    };
245	    if raw == windows_sys::Win32::Networking::WinSock::INVALID_SOCKET {
246	        return Err(webbluetooth_core::Error::Network(format!(
247	            "could not create RFCOMM listener: {}",
248	            last_error()
249	        )));
250	    }
251	    let socket = unsafe { std::net::TcpStream::from_raw_socket(raw as RawSocket) };
252	    let address = SockAddrBth {
253	        address_family: AF_BTH as u16,
254	        bt_addr: 0,
255	        service_class_id: unsafe { std::mem::zeroed() },
256	        port: channel as u32,
257	    };
258	    let bind_result = unsafe {
259	        windows_sys::Win32::Networking::WinSock::bind(
260	            raw,
261	            (&raw const address).cast(),
262	            std::mem::size_of_val(&address) as i32,
263	        )
264	    };
265	    let listen_result = unsafe { windows_sys::Win32::Networking::WinSock::listen(raw, 8) };
266	    if bind_result == windows_sys::Win32::Networking::WinSock::SOCKET_ERROR
267	        || listen_result == windows_sys::Win32::Networking::WinSock::SOCKET_ERROR
268	    {
269	        return Err(webbluetooth_core::Error::Network(format!(
270	            "could not bind RFCOMM channel {channel}: {}",
271	            last_error()
272	        )));
273	    }
274	    let socket = Arc::new(socket);
275	    let (tx, rx) = mpsc::unbounded();
276	    let accept_socket = socket.clone();
277	    std::thread::Builder::new()
278	        .name(format!("webbluetooth-windows-rfcomm-listener-{channel}"))
279	        .spawn(move || loop {
280	            let accepted = unsafe {
281	                windows_sys::Win32::Networking::WinSock::accept(
282	                    std::os::windows::io::AsRawSocket::as_raw_socket(&*accept_socket) as _,
283	                    std::ptr::null_mut(),
284	                    std::ptr::null_mut(),
285	                )
286	            };
287	            if accepted == windows_sys::Win32::Networking::WinSock::INVALID_SOCKET {
288	                break;
289	            }
290	            let accepted = unsafe { std::net::TcpStream::from_raw_socket(accepted as RawSocket) };
291	            let accepted = Arc::new(accepted);
292	            let (channel_sink, sink, incoming) = webbluetooth_core::l2cap::sink();
293	            let connected = Channel {
294	                socket: accepted,
295	                channel,
296	                peer: String::new(),
297	                closed: Mutex::new(None),
298	                stopped: Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false)),
299	                writing: Mutex::new(()),
300	            };
301	            spawn_reader(
302	                connected.socket.clone(),
303	                channel_sink,
304	                connected.stopped.clone(),
305	                channel,
306	            );
307	            if tx
308	                .unbounded_send(Ok(RfcommChannel::new(connected, sink, incoming)))
309	                .is_err()
310	            {
311	                break;
312	            }
313	        })
314	        .map_err(|error| webbluetooth_core::Error::Network(error.to_string()))?;
315	    Ok(RfcommListener {
316	        socket,
317	        incoming: rx,
318	    })
319	}

321	fn parse_address(value: &str) -> Result<u64, String> {
322	    let parts: Vec<_> = value.split(':').collect();
323	    if parts.len() != 6 {
324	        return Err("Bluetooth address needs six octets".into());
325	    }
326	    let mut address = 0u64;
327	    for part in parts {
328	        let octet = u8::from_str_radix(part, 16).map_err(|_| "invalid Bluetooth address")?;
329	        address = (address << 8) | u64::from(octet);
330	    }
331	    Ok(address)
332	}
333	
334	fn address_to_string(address: u64) -> String {
335	    (0..6)
336	        .rev()
337	        .map(|shift| format!("{:02X}", (address >> (shift * 8)) & 0xff))
338	        .collect::<Vec<_>>()
339	        .join(":")
340	}
341	
342	fn last_error() -> i32 {
343	    unsafe { windows_sys::Win32::Networking::WinSock::WSAGetLastError() }
344	}
345	
346	fn parse_guid(value: &str) -> Result<windows_sys::core::GUID, String> {
347	    let bytes = value.as_bytes();
348	    if bytes.len() != 36
349	        || bytes[8] != b'-'
350	        || bytes[13] != b'-'
351	        || bytes[18] != b'-'
352	        || bytes[23] != b'-'
353	    {
354	        return Err("service UUID must be a canonical GUID".into());
355	    }
356	    fn hex(slice: &[u8]) -> Result<u32, String> {
357	        u32::from_str_radix(std::str::from_utf8(slice).map_err(|_| "invalid UUID")?, 16)
358	            .map_err(|_| "invalid UUID".into())
359	    }
360	    let mut data4 = [0u8; 8];
361	    for (index, slot) in data4.iter_mut().enumerate() {
362	        *slot = u8::from_str_radix(
363	            std::str::from_utf8(&bytes[19 + index * 2..21 + index * 2])
364	                .map_err(|_| "invalid UUID")?,
365	            16,
366	        )
367	        .map_err(|_| "invalid UUID".to_string())?;
368	    }
369	    Ok(windows_sys::core::GUID {
370	        data1: hex(&bytes[0..8])?,
371	        data2: hex(&bytes[9..13])? as u16,
372	        data3: hex(&bytes[14..18])? as u16,
373	        data4,
374	    })
375	}

#### Thinking

Windows classic.rs is a REAL Winsock AF_BTH implementation: socket/connect/bind/listen/accept, client by channel AND by service UUID (SOCKADDR_BTH.serviceClassId — Windows does the SDP lookup natively when serviceClassId is set!), server listener. Not a stub. Note: it wraps raw sockets in TcpStream (a common hack), reader thread per channel. No WSAStartup call visible here — probably elsewhere (backend init). Also note: Windows server via `listen(channel)` binds a fixed channel but doesn't publish an SDP record (no WSASetService) — so Android connecting by UUID wouldn't find it. But for Liino's architecture (phone=server, desktop=client), Windows client by UUID is exactly what's needed. 

macOS classic.rs: paired_devices + find_device (address or name). No SDP query. Confirmed.

47	    pub fn new(server: Ref, channel: u8) -> Result<Self, String> {
48	        let stopped = Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false));
49	        let (tx, rx) = mpsc::unbounded();
50	        let accept_server = server.clone();
51	        let accept_stop = stopped.clone();
52	        std::thread::Builder::new()
53	            .name(format!("webbluetooth-android-rfcomm-{channel}"))
54	            .spawn(move || {
55	                let Some(runtime) = Runtime::get() else {
56	                    return;
57	                };
58	                let Ok(env) = runtime.env() else {
59	                    return;
60	                };
61	                while !accept_stop.load(Ordering::Acquire) {
62	                    let Ok(socket) = crate::ble::server_socket_accept(env, accept_server.as_ptr())

64	                        break;
65	                    };
66	                    if socket.is_null() {
67	                        break;
68	                    }
69	                    let result = from_accepted(socket, channel);
70	                    if tx.unbounded_send(result).is_err() {
71	                        break;
72	                    }
73	                }
74	                runtime.vm().detach();
75	            })
76	            .map_err(|error| error.to_string())?;
77	        Ok(Self {
78	            server,
79	            stopped,
80	            incoming: rx,
81	        })
82	    }
83	}

2	
3	- 状态：Accepted（依据“除蓝牙与 Flutter UI 外交给 MicYou”的产品约束）

6	## 背景
7	
8	MicYou 的移动端不是 Rust：
9	
10	- Android：`composeApp/.../audio/AudioEngine.kt` 使用 `AudioRecord`、Kotlin Opus（concentus）、`DatagramSocket`，并自带录音所有权与前台服务逻辑。
11	- iOS：`vendor/micyou-ios` 是 Swift 实现。
12	
13	liino 的移动端要把 Compose/SwiftUI 换成 Flutter UI。若把 MicYou 的采集/编码/传输搬到 Rust，会重写一套已经稳定的实现，与“维护量最小”冲突；若保留原生引擎，则移动端存在两套传输实现（Kotlin/Swift），需要与桌面 Rust 协议保持一致。
14	
15	## 决策（推荐）
16	
17	1. **移动端音频与传输仍由 MicYou 原生引擎负责**：采集、Opus、UDP/TCP、会话状态、前台服务都在 Kotlin/Swift。
18	2. Flutter 只通过 MethodChannel 下发控制（连接/断开/角色/参数）并接收节流后的状态事件；**PCM 不穿越 Flutter 通道**。
19	3. 移动端不通过 FRB 跑音频引擎；`liino_api` 在 Android 上只用于非实时能力（如网络接口、版本信息）或直接移除。
20	4. 蓝牙作为“新增传输”分别接入两端：Android 在 Kotlin 引擎里加 RFCOMM；桌面在 Rust `micyou-core` 里加 RFCOMM；共用同一套帧格式（见 ADR-0005）。
21	5. 桌面端保留 Rust 引擎（daemon 内嵌 `micyou-core`，见 ADR-0004）。
22	
23	## 代价
24	
25	- 没有“单一引擎代码库”；Android/iOS/桌面三端需要各自维护蓝牙与传输适配。
26	- Flutter 与原生之间需要定义稳定的控制/事件协议，并处理生命周期（后台、断连、权限）。
27	- 未来若要统一到 Rust，需要一次大迁移（可通过协议层先统一来降低风险）。
28	
29	## 备选方案
30	
31	- **全 Rust（FRB）**：统一语言与内存模型，但要重写 Kotlin 的录音所有权、Opus、前台服务与 iOS 音频会话，工期与回归风险最大；否决。
32	- **仅桌面复用 MicYou、移动端重写**：不满足维护量约束。
33	
34	## 需要先验证
35	
36	- 能否在不引入 Compose 的前提下，把 `DeviceDiscovery.kt` / `AudioEngine.kt` 作为 Gradle `sourceSets` 直接编译进 liino 的 Android 工程（而不是复制代码）。若依赖 Compose/ViewModel 过深，则退化为“只复用协议与流程，代码在 liino 内重写薄层”。
37	- MicYou Android 的 `AudioEngine` 是否可剥离 `Service`/通知依赖，仅保留引擎。

30:## Bluetooth Classic and RFCOMM
31-
32-The standard-shaped API remains Bluetooth LE/GATT. Bluetooth Classic support is
33-opt-in through the `classic` feature so applications can distinguish native
34:extensions from the Web Bluetooth surface. RFCOMM is a separate `rfcomm`
35-feature, which implies `classic`; its current implementation uses Linux's
36:`AF_BLUETOOTH` RFCOMM sockets.
37-
38-The separate `apple-classic` feature is the macOS IOBluetooth backend. It is
39-intentionally not enabled by `classic`: CoreBluetooth remains LE-only, and
40:Classic on a Mac means linking a second framework. `rfcomm` does enable it,
41:because asking for RFCOMM on a Mac is asking for IOBluetooth. It cannot be provided on
42-iOS, tvOS, watchOS, visionOS, or browser targets, none of which have
43-IOBluetooth.
44-
45:With `rfcomm` enabled, macOS has RFCOMM client channels. Two things about it differ from every other platform, and both come
46-from CoreBluetooth and IOBluetooth being separate frameworks that share
47-nothing:
48-
49-* **A device is found by address or by name, not by its `BluetoothDevice`
50-  id.** CoreBluetooth hides the address behind a per-host UUID that
51:  IOBluetooth has never heard of. `Bluetooth::open_rfcomm_channel(address,
52-  channel)` takes an address — `Bluetooth::paired_classic_devices()` lists
53:  them — and `BluetoothDevice::open_rfcomm_channel(channel)` bridges a
54-  dual-mode device by matching its name against the paired devices, which is
55-  a heuristic: two paired devices with one name cannot be told apart.
56-* **Events arrive on the main thread's run loop.** IOBluetooth delivers
57:  every RFCOMM callback — the open completing, each chunk of data, the peer
58-  closing — there, whichever thread opened the channel. An app keeps that run
59-  loop turning; a command-line program has to (`CFRunLoopRun`, or
60-  `CFRunLoopRunInMode` in a loop, on the main thread) and do its work on
61:  another thread, as `examples/rfcomm_macos.rs` does. Where it does not, the
62-  open fails with an error that says so, rather than returning a channel that
63-  can send but never receives.
64-* **The process needs Bluetooth permission of the Classic kind.** The device
65-  must be paired in System Settings first, and the open fails with
66-  `kIOReturnNotPermitted` unless the binary carries the
67-  `com.apple.security.device.bluetooth` entitlement — on recent macOS, from
68-  inside a signed `.app` bundle. Listing paired devices needs neither.

106-`ECONNREFUSED` and nothing else.

let input = Thread {
    let handle = FileHandle.standardInput
    while true {
        let data = handle.availableData
        if data.isEmpty {
            _ = channel.close()
            exit(0)
        }
        let written: IOReturn = data.withUnsafeBytes { buffer in
            guard let base = buffer.baseAddress else { return kIOReturnError }
            return channel.writeSync(

                length: UInt16(data.count)
            )
        }

mod bluetooth;

use ipc::{
    default_ipc_endpoint, parse_ipc_line, IpcRequest, IpcResponse, MAX_IPC_FRAME_BYTES,
    MAX_IPC_QUEUE_DEPTH,
};
use liino_core::{ResolvedRole, RoleMode, TransportType};
use liino_engine::presence::{Presence, PresenceConfig};
use liino_engine::stats::NetworkStats;
use liino_platform::{enriched_capabilities, probe_current_platform, VirtualMicStatus};
use tokio::io::{AsyncBufReadExt, AsyncWriteExt, BufReader};
use tokio::sync::{mpsc, oneshot, watch};

struct DaemonState {
    role_mode: RoleMode,
    active_transport: String,
    is_running: bool,
    stats: NetworkStats,
    presence: Option<Presence>,
    bluetooth: Option<bluetooth::BluetoothLink>,
}

impl Default for DaemonState {
    fn default() -> Self {
        let stats = NetworkStats::default();
        stats.set_audio_info(48_000, 1);
        let caps = enriched_capabilities();
        let role = caps
            .resolve_role(RoleMode::Auto)
            .unwrap_or_else(|_| caps.default_role());
        let presence = Presence::start(PresenceConfig {
            name: host_name(),
            platform: caps.platform_name.clone(),
            role: resolved_role_str(role).to_string(),
            transports: caps
                .supported_transports
                .iter()
                .map(|transport| transport_str(*transport))
                .collect(),
        })
        .map_err(|error| eprintln!("[liino-daemon] presence disabled: {error}"))
        .ok();
        Self {
            role_mode: RoleMode::Auto,
            active_transport: "lan_wifi".to_string(),
            is_running: false,
            stats,
            presence,
            bluetooth: None,
        }
    }
}

fn host_name() -> String {
    std::env::var("HOSTNAME")
        .or_else(|_| std::env::var("COMPUTERNAME"))
        .unwrap_or_else(|_| "liino desktop".to_string())
}

fn transport_str(transport: TransportType) -> String {
    match transport {
        TransportType::LanWifi => "lan_wifi",
        TransportType::Usb => "usb",
        TransportType::BluetoothRfcomm => "bluetooth_rfcomm",
    }
    .to_string()
}

struct QueuedCommand {
    req: IpcRequest,
    reply: oneshot::Sender<IpcResponse>,
}

fn role_mode_str(mode: RoleMode) -> &'static str {
    match mode {
        RoleMode::Auto => "auto",
        RoleMode::Sender => "sender",
        RoleMode::Receiver => "receiver",
    }

# ───────────────────────── sccache：跨仓复用编译产物 ─────────────────────────
#
# 为什么值得接（本机 2026-10-04 实测，sccache 0.18.0）：
#   - cargo clean 后同参数重编：Cache hits 18 / misses 0。
#   - **同一份源码复制到别的绝对目录再编：25 命中 / 2 未命中** —— 未命中的是本地 crate 自己，
#     依赖全部命中。所以跨仓复用是真的，不需要（也不该）共用 target 目录。
#   - 七仓 dev 默认开 incremental，但 cargo 只对**workspace 自己的 crate** 开 incremental，
#     依赖仍按非增量编 → 依赖照样进缓存。stats 里那些 Non-cacheable 就是本地 crate 本身
#     （reasons: crate-type 8 / missing input 4）。

Build-only evidence for the ADR-0005 re-evaluation; running it touches the\n//! radio and may trigger a TCC prompt, so it is left to the user.\n//!\n//!   bt-spike                # list paired classic devices\n//!   bt-spike <addr> <ch>    # open RFCOMM channel, print incoming bytes\n\nuse std::sync::mpsc;\nuse std::time::Duration;\n\nunsafe extern \"C\" {\n    fn CFRunLoopRunInMode(mode: *const std::ffi::c_void, seconds: f64, ret: bool) -> i32;\n    static kCFRunLoopDefaultMode: *const std::ffi::c_void;\n}\n\nfn main() -> webbluetooth::Result<()> {\n    let (done_tx, done) = mpsc::channel();\n    std::thread::spawn(move || {\n        let _ = done_tx.send(futures_executor::block_on(run()));\n    });\n    loop {\n        match done.recv_timeout(Duration::ZERO) {\n            Ok(result) => return result,\n            Err(mpsc::RecvTimeoutError::Disconnected) => return Ok(()),\n            Err(mpsc::RecvTimeoutError::Timeout) => {}\n        }\n        unsafe { CFRunLoopRunInMode(kCFRunLoopDefaultMode, 0.1, false) };\n    }\n}\n\nasync fn run() -> webbluetooth::Result<()> {\n    use webbluetooth::stream::StreamExt;\n    use webbluetooth::Bluetooth;\n\n    let bluetooth = Bluetooth::shared();\n    let paired = bluetooth.paired_classic_devices().await?;\n\n    let mut args = std::env::args().skip(1);\n    let Some(address) = args.next() else {\n        println!(\"{} paired classic device(s):\", paired.len());\n        for device in &paired {\n            println!(\n                \"  {}  {}\",\n                device.address.map(|a| a.to_string()).unwrap_or_default(),\n                device.name.as_deref().unwrap_or(\"(unnamed)\"),\n            );\n        }\n        return Ok(());\n    };\n    let channel: u8 = args.next().and_then(|a| a.parse().ok()).unwrap_or(1);\n\n    println!(\"opening RFCOMM channel {channel} on {address}…\");\n    let rfcomm = bluetooth.open_rfcomm_channel(&address, channel).await?;\n    println!(\"open. Ctrl-C to stop.\");\n\n    let mut incoming = rfcomm.take_incoming().expect(\"first take\");\n    while let Some(bytes) = incoming.next().await {\n        println!(\"{} B\", bytes.len());\n    }\n    println!(\"closed: {:?}\", rfcomm.closed());\n    Ok(())\n}",
